title: feat(app-shell): publish readEnvelopeFailureText, and read the agent-key failure through it (objectui#7980)
body:
Fixes #7980

Publish `readEnvelopeFailureText` from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s public entry, and have the
console's agent-key generator read the ADR-0112 failure envelope through it.

**Ruling of record: option B** — objectui#7980 comment 5583988475, a maintainer ruling
relayed by the director seat (decision batch #91, 2026-09-08), verbatim: «Export the
already-pinned pure function; the console reads `userMessage` (marked channel), then
`message`, with `code` appended, exactly as `apiErrorEnvelope.test.ts` pins. ⛔ A refused;
⛔ C refused.» Option A (a local copy in `apps/console`) is refused by name, and the
withdrawn 裁决 on comment 5597562427 is void per 5597586378.

## What was wrong

The Integrations page read a refused key mint as `json?.error?.message` and stopped, so two
DECLARED things never reached the developer:

- **`error.userMessage`** — the producer's #9934 marked channel, whose presence IS the
  marking. The producing door substitutes the generic `Internal server error` into
  `message` in the 5xx band while the mark rides through untouched, so a marked 500/503
  showed the developer the generic sentence and discarded the specific one written for
  them. Nothing invalid was displayed, which is what made the loss quiet.
- **`error.code`**, which never reached the surface at all.

The thrown string lands in `setError(...)` and IS the whole report the developer gets.

## The change

- `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` — one new named export, `readEnvelopeFailureText`.
- `apps/console/src/pages/developer/AgentConnectSection.tsx` — the `!res.ok` arm reads the
  envelope through the shared rule; `??`, not `||`, because the helper answers `null` for a
  prose-less body and that `null` is exactly the signal to state this caller's own fallback.
- A call-site pin, plus a `minor` / `patch` changeset.

The function itself is untouched. objectui#7959 kept it off the public entry as **scope
restraint** — that card's file surface was `packages/app-shell/**` — not as a ruling that it
should stay private.

## The Clause-② surface, measured rather than asserted

The dispatch's 前提 was that exporting this one already-pinned pure function is the WHOLE of
the surface change. Measured on the built type surface, `packages/app-shell/dist/index.d.ts`:

```
export { readEnvelopeFailureText } from './utils/apiErrorEnvelope.js';
export declare function readEnvelopeFailureText(payload: unknown): string | null;
```

- **No new type.** The signature is `unknown` in, `string | null` out — both primitives.
- **No transitive re-export and no module side effect.** `utils/apiErrorEnvelope.ts` imports
  nothing at all, and the module is not added to the package's `sideEffects` array
  (`check:side-effects-array` green).
- **`export` lines on the public entry: 83 to 84.** Exactly one, so the count is a reading.

The import direction was checked too, since the dispatch flagged it as an assumption:
`apps/console` already imports `@object-ui/app-shell`'s public entry in **41** source files,
so no dependency and no graph direction is new here. Option C is not put back on the table.

## Tests

All commands from the repo root, per this repo's vitest invocation rule. Evidence quoted
from the runs themselves; the suite numbers below are on the final commit `71966d740`.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/ packages/app-shell/src/utils/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` | `Test Files 372 passed (372)` · `Tests 4199 passed / 1 skipped` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/` (pre-merge) | `Test Files 665 passed (665)` · `Tests 6419 passed / 1 skipped` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell --filter @object-ui/console type-check` | both `Done` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell --filter @object-ui/console lint` | `0 errors` in both; **0** findings naming either changed file |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅ 3 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed … declares 1 changeset(s)` |

Gates run locally, each read from the gate's own verdict line, exit code captured before any
pipe: `check:control-bytes` `check:readme-exports` `check:eager-closure` `check:entry-guard`
`check:esm-specifiers` `check:self-import` `check:side-effects-array`
`check:unreferenced-sources` `check:published-dist` `check:published-tsconfig-exclude`
`check:phantom-deps` — **all exit 0**.

`check:eager-closure` is the one this diff could plausibly move, so it was measured against a
real `vite build` rather than skipped: aggregate closure **3484.2 KB / 3512.7 KB ceiling**,
and all four per-chunk ceilings green. Both that gate and `check:readme-exports` first
returned PREREQUISITE-NOT-MET on an unbuilt worktree and say so in as many words; the numbers
above are from the runs after the missing packages were built, not from the broken gauge.

`node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on this diff: **NOT GOVERNED** — 4 paths
checked against 5 governed surfaces, none matched.

### Ablation — the new pin can fail, and fails for the right reason

The console pin was proven capable of failing by reverting only the read, on the committed
tree, with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap holding the restore. Direction predicted before the run:
**turns red**. Observed: 4 of 5 red, and §4 stayed green — which is correct, because §4 is
the fallback case this change deliberately leaves byte-identical.

Mutation observability, anchored on the text actually being changed rather than on a
non-empty diffstat:

```
BEFORE  shared-read anchor: 1   legacy-read anchor: 1
AFTER   shared-read anchor: 0   legacy-read anchor: 2
HEAD blob ab99bff701c6bd8a3b59110e827ce565d0d5a6b5 -> on-disk 58d95999f49a5530bd37bb05481af4ae9cb5ded6
```

The §3 failure IS the card, reproduced:

```
§3 both — the marked 5xx shows the mark, and the generic sentence is gone
  Expected: "…Revoke one first. (INTERNAL_ERROR)"
  Received: "Internal server error"
```

Restore leg proven by BYTES, not by an exit code: `git checkout HEAD -- path`, then
`git diff HEAD` empty and the on-disk blob back to `ab99bff70…`. No mutation survives, and no
ablation artefact is left in the tree.

**Why no rebuild leg is needed for this pair:** the root vitest config aliases
`@object-ui/app-shell` to `packages/app-shell/src`, so the console test resolves the helper
through source and the mutation is observed directly. The `dist/` surface was verified
separately, by `apps/console`'s own `tsc` — which has no `paths` mapping and therefore reads
`@object-ui/app-shell` through `node_modules` at `dist/index.d.ts`. That typecheck is a real
cross-package reverse verification of the new export: it was RED before the export existed
and is green now.

## 验收备注

- **`origin/main` was merged**, and it did conflict. PR objectui#8787 (objectui#8782) landed
  on `AgentConnectSection.tsx` mid-run and split the two failure arms. The conflict is
  resolved in favour of **their** structure verbatim — both arms, their comment, their new
  keyless-success sentence — with only the prose read inside the `!res.ok` arm swapped for
  the shared rule. Their new pin (`AgentConnectSection.keylessSuccess-8782.test.tsx`) is
  untouched and green.
- **The keyless-success arm is out of scope and was left alone**, and this PR deliberately
  pins nothing about it. A pin of that wording from here would be a tripwire on that card's
  work. It is called out in the test file's own header so the next reader does not add one.
- PR objectui#8789 (objectui#8051) also landed during the run; it touched `PackageFormDialog`,
  not the helper and not the public entry, so the export line remains this branch's only
  change to `index.ts`.
- `noted, not filed:` the dispatch brief recorded objectui#8787 as already landed. It was
  **open** when this branch was cut and merged during the run — a timing artefact of a moving
  `main`, not a defect in anything. Carrier: none needed; the merge above absorbs it.

## Landing

`Clause-②: yes` — a new export on a published index. Carrier `needs:contract-review` is on
both the card and this PR, and the review is owed on this diff before it enqueues.
`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` was measured unavailable (429) at dispatch, which per objectui#8069
comment 5594065532 gates the **review**, not the construction.

⛔ This stays a **draft**. Not flipped ready, no auto-merge armed, not enqueued — that is the
PM seat's call once a contract review is on record.
